Lesson 2 You have heard it said that reading brings knowledge, but this is partially false, for it greatly depends on that which you have chosen to read. Not all information results in the growth of knowledge. We must consider the source.
第二课 你一定听过「读书增长见识」这种说法。这话只对了一半，它极大地取决于你选择读的是什么。并非所有信息都能化作见识。我们必须考量来源。

This is particularly difficult when identifying relics and artifacts, for many stories revolve around them. Some are to be trusted, and others not, but can one decide?

	There exists an entire field of research for vetting authors, but this is nearly impossible with old tales.

在鉴定遗物与古器时，这一点尤为棘手，因为围绕它们的故事实在太多。有的可信，有的不可信，可你分辨得出来吗？

	甄别作者真伪本身已是一门专门的学问，但面对古老传说，这几乎无从下手。

One must let the artifact do the talking. It will either reveal truth in the tale, or show it to be false. To start, select a clay pot. Though adventurers have a penchant for smashing them on sight (a practice I find most disturbing), they are commonplace and sometimes carry interesting stories.

	The humble clay pot is more than just a vessel for carrying water, food or household goods.

得让古器自己开口。它要么印证传说为真，要么证明其为假。先挑一只陶罐吧。虽说冒险者总爱见一个砸一个（这种做派让我极不痛快），但陶罐最为常见，有时还承载着有趣的故事。

	朴实无华的陶罐，绝不只是盛水、装粮或搁家什的器皿。

It is a vessel for knowledge, for the lives of their owners can be found in the subtle details.

	Look for markings, such as scratches from daily use, damage or even intentional scrapes meant to signify something about the contents. Peer into these windows left for you. We will get to the contents soon enough, but for now observe only the outside.

它是知识的容器，主人的生活藏在细微的痕迹里。

	去找那些印记：日常使用留下的划痕、磕碰的缺口，甚至故意刮出的、标示罐中之物的痕记。透过这些为你留下的窗口往里看吧。我们很快就会讲到罐子里头，但眼下，只观察外侧。

Material, weight, coloring and wear and tear are all attributes to keep your focus on. They are indelibly linked, and form a pattern for the keen observer.

	Now take your time. Be with the piece for a time, and return to me with your findings. You have each been assigned a special piece. Do not break it! If you do, you will join me on the dig site for three weeks or until you replace it.

材质、重量、色泽、磨损，这些都值得你专注。它们彼此相系，在敏锐的观察者眼中自会构成规律。

	慢慢来。与你的器物待上一阵，再把发现带来见我。你们每人分到了一件特别的器物。别打碎它！否则，你就得跟我去发掘现场干上三周，或者直到你赔上一件为止。
